clue.text: Attribute correct sources of tax yearly

parts.note: correct as an adjective means proper, fitting

indicators.note: the sources of words are their opening letters, taken here from tax and yearly

explanation.surface: An accountant describing how to declare the taxman's annual dues properly.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic quality of something can be called one of its properties, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Friend with strange ideas for defensive structure

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of ideas are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A friend with unusual notions about building fortifications.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence of pointed stakes forming an enclosure or defence is a stockade, the same thing.

clue.text: Up in London, a growing newspaper, for example

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upward
in signals the letters are held within the run of words London a growing

explanation.surface: Up in the capital, a newspaper that is gaining readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks NAGRO from the words, and 'Up' turns them backwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is a publication voicing a party's views, called its mouthpiece; organ is the standard word for such a voice.

clue.text: Doctor learnt about hospital transport

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the H
to doctor something is to tamper with it, rearranging these letters

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A physician has studied how patients are moved to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges LEARNT to ENTRAL, and 'about' puts that around H. 'Transport' is the verb, to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone with joy is to captivate or enchant them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Dog brush

definitions.meaning: to dog someone is to follow them closely
the brush is the bushy rear appendage of a fox

explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is the verb sense; a fox's brush is the noun sense of the rear appendage.

clue.text: A club oddly needing workers to show discernment

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions, first and third, of the word club

parts.note: workers, the staff on a site, are men

explanation.surface: A sports club needs staff who can show good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight or shrewdness, a close synonym of discernment.

clue.text: Agents employing scoundrel needing small bugs

indicators.note: employing means the agency takes the scoundrel in, holding him inside

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of agents
a cad is a scoundrel
S is the clothing abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Spies hiring a rogue who needs small listening devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects of the order of true bugs that chirp loudly in summer are cicadas, so bugs covers them.

clue.text: Public communications service aimed for reform

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: for reform means the letters of aimed are reshaped

explanation.surface: A broadcasting service with an agenda to reform society.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers, television and radio reaching the general population collectively are the press and broadcasters.

clue.text: Moving slowly, issue raised at home beginning to grate

indicators.note: raised in a down clue lifts the word so it reads upward

parts.note: issue means offspring, here a son
in means at home

indicators.note: the beginning of grate is its first letter

explanation.surface: Creeping along, a grievance brought up at home starts to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat or car edging cautiously forward is said to be inching its way, poking its front forward.

clue.text: Striker's night playing in topless affair

definitions.note: something that strikes, as a bolt from a storm does

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the trimmed word
topless means the word loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: a brief affair is a fling

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of night are performing in a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer's night out spent in a scandalous fling with a topless partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' looks like a footballer, but it is the definition; the 's reads as 'is'. 'topless' and 'playing' work on the affair and the night, and 'in' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash from a thunderstorm famously strikes trees and buildings, so a striker is a playful description of it.

clue.text: Jokes about boy and right things to wear for best

indicators.note: about means the jokes go around the boy and the right

parts.note: gags are jokes
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Banter about a lad and the proper outfits for a special occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: One's smartest clothes, worn for special occasions, are informally one's finery.

clue.text: Selects actors seeing son featured in musical

indicators.note: featured in means the son appears within the musical's title

parts.note: Cats is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A director chooses performers after seeing a boy appear in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick performers for parts in a production is the verb sense of casting.

clue.text: Watch nurse have a go

parts.note: SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Telling a nurse to keep an eye out and make an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard posted on watch duty is a sentry; watch here is the noun for a lookout.

clue.text: Applause upset many a DIY-er

parts.note: to give someone a big hand is to applaud them

indicators.note: upset knocks the letters of many over into a new order

explanation.surface: Clapping annoys plenty of home-improvement enthusiasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does odd jobs and repairs around the house is a do-it-yourself type.

clue.text: Be angry over brief effort to get garden tool

indicators.note: over means the angry word goes over and around the shortened effort

parts.note: to simmer is to be quietly angry

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an effort is a try

explanation.surface: Fuming over a half-hearted attempt to buy something for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' shortens the effort and 'over' wraps the anger round it; 'Be angry' is a verb phrase, so its synonym is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimmer with a spinning nylon line for cutting grass edges; the name is a British trademark.

clue.text: Planned limited rides across area that's free of armed forces

indicators.note: across means the rearranged letters stretch over the A, holding it inside
planned suggests the letters are arranged afresh to a design

explanation.surface: Organised short excursions through a zone where no troops are allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planned' rearranges LIMITED RIDES, and 'across' puts that around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone from which military forces have been withdrawn by treaty is described as demilitarised.

clue.text: Plan page about the French national symbol

indicators.note: about here places the page beside the French article, coming around after it

parts.note: a plan of an area is a map
le is French for the
a leaf is a page of a book

explanation.surface: A design on the page concerning the French national emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The emblem on Canada's flag is the leaf of a sugar tree, the country's national symbol.

clue.text: Heavenly ale brewed around the outskirts of Rome

indicators.note: around means the rearranged ale encloses the other letters
brewed means the letters of ale are stirred up into a new order
the outskirts of Rome are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A divine beer brewed on the edge of the Eternal City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' gives EAL, which 'around' wraps about the clue's own 'the' plus the outskirts of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial or otherworldly, light and delicate as if not of this earth; a synonym.

clue.text: Out of form?

parts.note: a form is a school class, so someone out of their form without leave is skipping school

explanation.surface: A sports commentator remarking that a player has lost their touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of form' suggests poor sporting performance; here a form is a British school class, and the pupil is absent from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying away from school without permission is the familiar idiom for bunking off lessons.

clue.text: Entertainer's energy supporting painter

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the energy underneath, holding up the painter

parts.note: a painter is an artist
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A performer's vitality props up a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional performer, such as a singer or dancer, is a stage artiste.

clue.text: Broadcast shown again without pressure

indicators.note: without means the pressure letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a programme shown again is replayed
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A programme aired as a repeat without any pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a signal on or transmit it is to broadcast, a verb synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Bags of nameless pasta

indicators.note: nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: noodles are a kind of pasta

explanation.surface: Packets of unbranded pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags of something, in informal speech, means large amounts, and so does lots.

clue.text: Work possibly available in the long run?

definitions.meaning: extra hours of paid work beyond the normal shift
gradually, as time passes, read as two words

explanation.surface: Wondering whether there might be a job going eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra paid hours are offered when demand rises, and the phrase split in two means eventually.

clue.text: Fever seeing capital changing sides?

indicators.note: changing sides swaps the right for the left, R becoming L

parts.note: Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: A political fever as a capital city switches allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestilence such as bubonic disease brought high fever, so the illness stands for fever loosely.

clue.text: Piece in America about a love for fertiliser

indicators.note: about means the firearm goes around the letter A

parts.note: piece is American slang for a firearm
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A gun in the US wrapped around a love of manure.
explanation.definitionFit: Seabird or bat droppings, collected and used to enrich soil, are a natural manure.

clue.text: Duty one has to provide transport

parts.note: a duty is a tax
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A levy one must pay to supply transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab hired for a journey is a means of getting about, an example of transport.

clue.text: City shelter dropouts left empty

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: left empty means only the outer letters of dropouts remain, the inside removed

explanation.surface: A city refuge for drifters stands deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in West Yorkshire, England, named here only as a city.

clue.text: Servant rumoured to be after money is immediately available

indicators.note: after places the servant's word behind the money

parts.note: the ready is slang for cash

indicators.note: rumoured means the word is passed on by word of mouth, so it is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a maid is a female servant

explanation.surface: Gossip has it a servant chasing money is on hand straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prefabricated and supplied for instant use is called off-the-peg or ready-made.

clue.text: Moderate, generally after start of summer

indicators.note: after puts the adverb behind the opening letter
the start of summer is its first letter

parts.note: generally, as a rule, means often

explanation.surface: Weather tends to become milder once summer begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate something is to temper it or make it less harsh, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Violent offence at football reported in game

parts.note: wild behaviour is violent or unruly

indicators.note: reported means the word is said out loud, giving one of the same sound

parts.note: a foul is an infringement in a football match

explanation.surface: A vicious tackle in a match is written up by the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Game birds such as ducks and geese hunted for sport are called wild birds of this kind.
